events.description: Bombings in Saudi Arabia prompting stronger Saudi commitment against al-Qa'ida.
Casablanca bombings carried out by Salafiya Jihadia.
Detention of Ansar al-Islam's deputy leader in Iraq.
Tenet delivers Worldwide Threat testimony to Senate Select Committee on Intelligence.
Qadhafi reached out through British intelligence with an offer to abandon WMD pursuit.
Cargo of centrifuge parts bound for Libya seized after a tip.
Libyans admitted nuclear weapons program and gave access to Scud B forces during December visit.
Constitutional Loya Jirga ratified Afghan constitution.
Completion of the Kabul to Kandahar road.
Vajpayee's 'hand of friendship' initiative toward Pakistan.
Bali terrorist attacks linked to Jemaah Islamiya.
Jakarta Marriott Hotel attack linked to JI.
Bali terrorist attacks linked to JI suspects.
Afghan opium crop doubled.
Salafiya Jihadia carried out the Casablanca bombings.
12 May bombings in Saudi Arabia prompting stronger Saudi commitment against al-Qa'ida.
Tenet testifies on worldwide threat before the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence.
Khalid Shaykh Muhammad sent Hambali $50,000 for Southeast Asia operations.
Over the past 18 months key al-Qa'ida leaders including KSM, Nashiri, Abu Zubayda, Hasan Ghul, Harithi, al-Makki and Hambali were killed or captured.
Qadhafi reached out via British intelligence offering to abandon WMD pursuit.
Cargo of centrifuge parts bound for Libya was seized following a tip.
By the end of the December visit the Libyans admitted nuclear weapons and CW programs and disclosed Scud facilities.
North Korea announced withdrawal from the NPT and expelled IAEA inspectors.
North Korea began a unilateral long-range missile launch moratorium.
Pyongyang intercepted a US reconnaissance aircraft in international airspace as tensions over the nuclear program built.
Iran continued R&D on longer-range ballistic missiles and SLVs.
Tenet discusses the roll-up of AQ Khan's network as a counter-proliferation success.
Qadhafi decides to abandon WMD and reaches out via British intelligence.
Cargo of centrifuge parts bound for Libya seized after a tip-off.
US and British intelligence officers visit Libya; Libyans admit nuclear weapons program and disclose WMD facilities.
Planned return of sovereignty to an interim Iraqi government.
Peak of daily attacks on US and Coalition forces in Iraq.
Saddam Hussein captured; he is now in prison and the Coalition has killed or apprehended all but 10 of his 54 key cronies.
Detention of Ansar al-Islam's deputy leader, setting back its umbrella ambitions.
Khalid Shaykh Muhammad sent Hambali $50,000 for operations in Southeast Asia.
September 11 attacks, referred to as al-Qa'ida's 'shining moment'.
Planned return of sovereignty to an interim Iraqi government by 1 July.
Saddam captured; coalition killed or apprehended all but 10 of 54 key cronies.
Bali terrorist attacks linked to JI.
Colombian officials captured the two most senior FARC leaders ever in the last two months.
Colombian Army decimated several FARC military units.
Constitutional Loya Jirga ratified new Afghan constitution.
Iranian elections won by hardliners; at least eight killed in election-related violence.
Vajpayee's "hand of friendship" initiative toward Pakistan.
North Korea intercepted a US reconnaissance aircraft in international airspace (early last year).
Constitutional Loya Jirga ratified a new Afghan constitution.
Continued attacks by the Taliban, al-Qa'ida and Hikmatyar followers against the Afghan Transitional Authority in the south and east.

key_claims: Al-Qa'ida's central leadership has been seriously damaged but remains committed to attacking the US homeland.
Key al-Qa'ida leaders in logistics, planning, finance and training were killed or captured in the prior 18 months, including leadership in Pakistani urban areas.
Al-Qa'ida has become a loose collection of regional networks that operate autonomously, though KSM funded Hambali's Southeast Asia operations.
Bin Ladin has gone deep underground and the US is hunting him in remote regions.
Groups like IMU, LIFG, Ansar al-Islam and the Zarqawi network are the next wave of threat, autonomous from Bin Ladin.
President Musharraf of Pakistan is described as an indispensable ally targeted by assassins.
Intelligence penetration of AQ Khan's worldwide network was a major counter-proliferation success.
Khan's network offered one-stop shopping for enrichment technology and weapons design information.
North Korea is believed to pursue uranium enrichment using technology provided by Khan.
Iran supports SCIRI and the Badr Organization, which have gained positions in the Iraqi police.
Libya agreed to disarm after nine months of negotiations leveraged by US and British intelligence.
The Taliban is far from able to challenge the Karzai government but can undermine public confidence through insecurity in the south and east.
The Taliban, al-Qa'ida and Hikmatyar's followers were the main enemies of the Afghan Transitional Authority in 2003 and sought to derail Bonn.
Fahim Khan was judged to be keeping his Panjshiri supporters in line behind the Bonn process.
Taliban remnants seek to drive aid organizations from areas that most need them and to attack US and Coalition forces.
Indonesian authorities arrested more than 100 JI suspects, but elections blunted the crackdown.
About 50 countries have stateless zones, and in half of them terrorist groups are thriving.
Al-Qa'ida and the Taliban operate in the Afghanistan-Pakistan border area, a well-known stateless zone.
Terrorists driven from safe havens will seek new remote, rugged regions beyond government reach.
The doubling of the Afghan opium crop in 2003 shows narcotics can exploit absent government authority.
Drug trafficking is an important funding source for local terrorist groups in Afghanistan and Colombia.
India-Pakistan normalization progressed, but militant infiltration across the LOC remains a watched indicator.
